cat > /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guillaumeloulier-PhpstormProjects-oss-elephc--claude-worktrees-streams-csv-signature/c8dbe38f-1f79-484f-9b83-62bacab9ca56/scratchpad/uv/msg20.txt <<'EOF'
fix(checker): ZipArchive was registered behind a gate that could never open for it

`inject_builtin_spl_classes` inserts `ZipArchive`, but it only runs when
`program_may_reference_spl` says the program can reach one of the classes it registers — and that
scan reads `SPL_CLASS_NAMES` and `PHAR_CLASS_NAMES`, neither of which names it. So `new
ZipArchive()` got "Undefined class: ZipArchive" from a compiler that HAS the class, fully
implemented, with its own read surface measured against php. Five tests were red for a missing
string.

The name is added. What is worth more than the name is the GATE that now reads both sides: every
class the registration inserts must be reachable by the scan that decides whether to register.
Two lists that have to agree and nothing comparing them is how this survived — the class existed,
the tests for it existed, and no diagnostic anywhere pointed at the list.

It found a second name on its first run: `__ElephcAppendIteratorArrayIterator`, a synthetic the
registration builds for `AppendIterator`'s internal storage. That one is excluded deliberately and
by a rule rather than by name — a `__Elephc` prefix cannot be written in PHP source, so it is
unreachable BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by omission.

`ZIP_CLASS_NAMES` is its own list rather than an entry in `SPL_CLASS_NAMES`, because ZIP is not
SPL; what it shares with Phar is only the registration that inserts it.
EOF
